solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Quiet country with hot area for predatory fish (7)

blocks.note: h = hot, as on a tap

annotation.surface: A hush falls over a sultry land where something with teeth lurks in the water.
annotation.walkthrough: Four short pieces simply laid end to end; 'with' just strings them together.
annotation.definitionFit: The piranha is the South American river fish famous for its sharp teeth and appetite.

entries.clue: Dickensian illustrator purchasing house in Zurich first of all (4)

indicatorNotes.first of all: the first of each of all the words that precede it, so take every initial

annotation.surface: An artist from Dickens's circle is out house-hunting in Switzerland.
annotation.walkthrough: Phiz was the pen name of Hablot K. Browne, who drew the pictures for many of Dickens's novels.
annotation.definitionFit: Phiz illustrated The Pickwick Papers and other Dickens novels, so he is the Dickensian illustrator by name.

entries.clue: Revised text about religious feast, as released (9)

indicatorNotes.released: something released is let go, so the letters AS are let go from the feast's name

blocks.note: ASCENSION, the feast of Christ's ascent, without AS

annotation.surface: An editor reworks a document about a church festival.
annotation.walkthrough: 'As' looks like a conjunction ('as released') but it is the pair of letters to remove from the feast.
annotation.definitionFit: A recension is a revised edition of a text, especially an old one worked over by scholars.

entries.clue: Tips from new commander overwhelmed a sergeant, say (3-12,7)

indicatorNotes.Tips from: the tips of words are their ends, here their first letters

blocks.note: N, the tip of 'new', and the N of NCO written out in full
C, the tip of 'commander', and the C of NCO written out in full
O, the tip of 'overwhelmed', and the O of NCO written out in full

annotation.surface: A newly arrived commander swamps a sergeant with advice.
annotation.walkthrough: The three initials spell NCO, the standard abbreviation, and the answer is that abbreviation expanded; an unusual step worth noticing.
annotation.definitionFit: A sergeant is the classic non-commissioned officer, ranking above the privates but holding no commission, so the definition is by example.

entries.clue: A requirement to digest one’s cake flavouring (7)

indicatorNotes.to digest: to digest food is to take it inside you, so the requirement takes the next piece inside

blocks.note: one's = I'S, I as the Roman one plus the 's

annotation.surface: A recipe insists you must eat something before tasting the cake.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is all about eating cake, which hides that 'digest' is purely a placing instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: Aniseed, with its liquorice taste, is a traditional flavouring for cakes and biscuits.

entries.clue: Quirky law from east binding that chap thus (9)

indicatorNotes.from east: an across entry read from the east starts at the right-hand end, so it runs backwards
indicatorNotes.binding: binding wraps round something, so the reversed word wraps round the middle

annotation.surface: An odd statute arrives from the Orient to tie some fellow down.
annotation.walkthrough: Sic is the Latin 'thus' printed in brackets after a quoted error, and a staple for 'thus' in crosswords.
annotation.definitionFit: Whimsical means playfully quirky or fanciful, a plain synonym.

entries.clue: Necessary funds enclosed in top half of wallet? (11)

indicatorNotes.in: the enclosed word sits in the half-wallet, surrounded by it

blocks.note: the first three of WALLET's six letters
'herewith' is how a formal letter says something is enclosed

annotation.surface: Cash needed is tucked into the upper part of a billfold.
annotation.walkthrough: In a down entry the top half is the first half. 'Enclosed' looks like the container signal, but it is the piece being contained.
annotation.definitionFit: The wherewithal is the money or means needed for something, and the question mark nods to money in a wallet.

entries.clue: Unsuitability of snap I sent out (9)

indicatorNotes.out: sent out means dispersed, so the letters scatter and regroup

annotation.surface: Someone regrets a photograph they posted that was not fit to share.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sent out' reads as posting a photo; only 'out' is the instruction, and 'sent' is fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Inapt means unsuitable, so inaptness is the noun for unsuitability.

entries.clue: Eg, Leicester’s novel record? (5)

blocks.note: She, the novel by H. Rider Haggard
an EP is an extended-play record

annotation.surface: A question about some literary or musical work from the city of Leicester.
annotation.walkthrough: Leicester looks like the English city, but the Leicester Longwool is a breed of farm animal; 's is 'is'.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Leicester is one breed among the many kinds of this woolly farm animal.

entries.clue: Builders may use one managing pit (6,5)

blocks.note: the stone of a fruit is its pit

annotation.surface: Builders may use something to run a mine or quarry.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pit' suggests a mine, but here it is the hard stone of a cherry or plum.
annotation.definitionFit: A coping stone is the top stone of a wall, laid by builders to shed rain.

entries.clue: Hang about, departing at last in ocean-going vessel (6)

indicatorNotes.at last: at the last means at the end, so take the final letter of 'departing'
indicatorNotes.in: the letter is put in the vessel, like a passenger on board

annotation.surface: A passenger dawdles on board as the ship is about to sail.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Departing' fits the ship's sailing, which disguises that only its final letter is wanted.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to hang about somewhere is to stay on, slow to leave.

entries.clue: Muslim market? It’s substantially like this country (4)

blocks.note: so = like this, and so = very
the paper's own country, the United Kingdom

annotation.surface: A visitor finds an Arab bazaar surprisingly like home.
annotation.walkthrough: Together it reads 'so UK', slang for 'very British', which is what the surface claims the market is.
annotation.definitionFit: A souk is an open-air market in an Arab or Muslim country.

entries.clue: Old woman carrying in a simple wind instrument (7)

indicatorNotes.carrying: the woman carries the next word, holding it within her

blocks.note: as printed, carried inside the name

annotation.surface: An elderly lady brings along a basic instrument to blow.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Old woman' wants to be one unit, MA or CRONE, but it splits into O plus a name.
annotation.definitionFit: An ocarina is a small egg-shaped clay flute with finger holes, about as simple as wind instruments get.

entries.clue: Unit of distance? More like temperature, surprisingly (9)

indicatorNotes.surprisingly: the letters end up in an unexpected, surprising order

annotation.surface: Someone asks about a measure of length and gets a weather report.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark ends the definition and makes 'More like' look like a reply, not fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A kilometre is a thousand metres, the metric unit for road distances.

entries.clue: Dodgson’s work reportedly disconcerted the Mirror? (7,3,7-5)

indicatorNotes.reportedly: what is reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the word is heard, not spelt

blocks.note: threw = disconcerted, as in 'it threw me'

annotation.surface: Lewis Carroll's book is said to have unsettled a tabloid newspaper.
annotation.walkthrough: Dodgson is Charles Dodgson, whose pen name was Lewis Carroll. The Mirror is also a British tabloid, which the capital M plays on.
annotation.definitionFit: Through the Looking-Glass is Carroll's 1871 sequel to Alice in Wonderland, so it is literally Dodgson's work.

entries.clue: Selfish person in the know worried about scam (13)

indicatorNotes.about: about means around, so the person goes around the scam

blocks.note: an insider knows what's going on
ate = worried, as in 'what's eating you?'

annotation.surface: A self-centred insider frets over a fraud.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Worried about' reads as one phrase, but 'about' belongs with the scam and 'worried' is its own piece.
annotation.definitionFit: A near-synonym: someone inconsiderate gives no thought to others, which is selfish behaviour.

entries.clue: Drink before dance? It’s what a boxer may have (9)

annotation.definition: It’s what a boxer may have

indicatorNotes.before: before means ahead of, so the drink comes first in the answer

blocks.note: a ball is a formal dance

annotation.surface: A cocktail before the dance, as a fighter might enjoy.
annotation.walkthrough: A boxer does have a punch as well, which is why the definition works both ways.
annotation.definitionFit: A punchball is an inflated ball on a stand that boxers practise hitting.

entries.clue: Essential to secure company for rambling (10)

indicatorNotes.to secure: to secure something is to hold it fast, here by enclosing it

annotation.surface: Walkers are told it is vital to find companions for a hike.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rambling' reads as country walking, but the definition is rambling speech.
annotation.definitionFit: Rambling talk wanders without logic, i.e. it is incoherent.

entries.clue: Din god and devil initially investigated with sign of hesitation (11)

indicatorNotes.initially: at the start, so take the first letter of 'investigated'

blocks.note: Pan, the Greek god of the wild

annotation.surface: A racket as a god and a devil are looked into, with a hesitant pause.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Initially' governs only 'investigated'; the devil stays whole. Milton coined the word for the capital of Hell, which suits the god-and-devil surface.
annotation.definitionFit: Pandemonium is wild uproar and noise, a din.

entries.clue: Man with papers and style (5)

annotation.surface: A well-dressed gentleman carries his newspapers.
annotation.walkthrough: Man is the Isle of Man, a British Crown dependency in the Irish Sea, abbreviated IOM.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom is a characteristic style, as in a composer's musical idiom.

entries.clue: Popular drink yours truly would find tasteless (7)

blocks.note: a sip is a small drink
I'D = I would, yours truly being the speaker

annotation.surface: A trendy drink that the writer would find bland.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Yours truly' is crossword-speak for the setter, I, and 'would' supplies the contraction.
annotation.definitionFit: Insipid means lacking flavour, tasteless.

entries.clue: Like automated vehicles, oddly red and silver — and small (10)

indicatorNotes.oddly: in an odd, strange way, so the letters are arranged strangely

annotation.surface: A description of self-driving cars in a red and silver livery.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' often means take the odd letters; here it just means scramble.
annotation.definitionFit: An automated vehicle steers itself with nobody behind the wheel, so it lacks a driver.

entries.clue: French museum’s door or window slats (7)

annotation.definitionNote: the first sense is a possessive

blocks.note: the great Paris art museum, in the possessive
angled slats set in a door or window

annotation.surface: The Louvre in Paris has shuttered doors and windows.
annotation.walkthrough: The apostrophe is ignored in the grid, so the museum's name and the slats spell the same.
annotation.definitionFit: Louvres are sets of angled slats letting air through a door or window; the museum's name in the possessive spells the same.

entries.clue: Agent disturbed by swindles, overcome with horror (6)

indicatorNotes.disturbed by: someone disturbed by a visitor is interrupted, so the next piece breaks in

blocks.note: to have someone = to trick them, as in 'you've been had'

annotation.surface: A secret agent is horrified to discover he has been cheated.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Disturbed' tempts you to an anagram, but here it means interrupted.
annotation.definitionFit: Aghast means struck with horror or shock.

entries.clue: Taken in by bulky catalogue, head of authority who’s resigned (8)

annotation.definitionNote: read as 'one who's resigned', a noun

indicatorNotes.Taken in by: something taken in by a pair is enclosed between them
indicatorNotes.head of: the head is the top, so take the first letter of 'authority'

annotation.surface: An official's name is caught up in a thick directory as he steps down.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Resigned' looks like quitting a job, but here it means accepting fate.
annotation.definitionFit: A fatalist accepts that events are predetermined, resigned to whatever comes.

entries.clue: Composer’s offspring disheartened guests with German hotel (9)

indicatorNotes.disheartened: the heart of 'guests' is removed, leaving its outside letters

blocks.note: H = hotel in the phonetic alphabet

annotation.surface: A composer's child has lost heart as guests go to a German hotel.
annotation.walkthrough: 'With' looks like a joining word, but 'with German' asks for the German word for with.
annotation.definitionFit: A songsmith is someone who crafts songs, the -smith marking a maker as in wordsmith, so a composer.

entries.clue: Offender to begin with breaking into pub cash? Not guilty (8)

indicatorNotes.to begin with: at the beginning, so take the first letter of 'offender'
indicatorNotes.breaking into: a burglar breaking into a place gets inside it, so the letter goes inside

blocks.note: a cent, a small sum of money

annotation.surface: A burglar breaks into a pub's till, but claims innocence.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a crime, and the answer is the plea.
annotation.definitionFit: The verdict 'not guilty' declares the accused innocent in law.

entries.clue: Old Italian coin, something chewed over by bankers ultimately (5)

indicatorNotes.by: by means beside, so the banker's letter stands next to the rest
indicatorNotes.ultimately: in the end, so take the last letter of 'bankers'

annotation.surface: Bankers mull over an antique coin.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Chewed over' looks like one phrase meaning thought about; it splits in two.
annotation.definitionFit: The scudo was a silver coin used in Italian states until the 19th century.

entries.clue: Entertainer’s treat is misguided (7)

indicatorNotes.misguided: the letters are led wrongly into a new order

annotation.surface: A performer's indulgence is ill-judged.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is' joining definition to wordplay; the second 'is' is part of the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: An artiste is a professional entertainer such as a singer or dancer.

entries.clue: Colossal volley? Not entirely (5)

indicatorNotes.Not entirely: the answer is only part of the words shown, never the whole of them

annotation.surface: A huge barrage turns out to be less than complete.
annotation.walkthrough: The setter uses 'volley' twice on purpose: it is the definition and also supplies the last two hidden letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A salvo is a burst of simultaneous gunfire, the military sense of volley.

entries.clue: Die by river, clutching one tropical bloom? (7,6)

indicatorNotes.clutching: to clutch something is to hold it tight, so the first piece holds the next inside

blocks.note: a flower is something that flows, a river

annotation.surface: Someone dies beside a river, holding a single exotic flower.
annotation.walkthrough: The river as 'something that flows' is a crossword favourite. 'By' only places it next to the rest.
annotation.definitionFit: The passion flower is a climbing plant with striking blooms, native to tropical America.

entries.clue: A flightless bird once associated with south Pacific state (5)

blocks.note: the moa, an extinct flightless bird of New Zealand

annotation.surface: An extinct bird is linked to an island nation in the southern Pacific.
annotation.walkthrough: 'South' looks like part of 'south Pacific' but it is a piece of wordplay; the definition is just 'Pacific state'.
annotation.definitionFit: Samoa is an independent island state in the South Pacific.

entries.clue: Communicate quietly with that man’s reputation rising (7)

indicatorNotes.rising: in a down entry, rising means reading from the bottom upwards, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: REP (reputation, as in street cred) turned upwards

annotation.surface: A man speaks softly as his standing improves.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rising' reads as a reputation improving, but in a down clue it turns the word upside down.
annotation.definitionFit: To whisper is to speak under the breath, the softest way to communicate aloud.

entries.clue: English celebrity escorted across lake, given a coat (9)

indicatorNotes.across: stretched across something means spanning it, so the escort word spans the lake letter

blocks.note: a big name is a celebrity
l = lake, inside the escort word

annotation.surface: An English star is taken over a lake and handed a jacket.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Given a coat' reads as clothing, but it means a coat of enamel or paint.
annotation.definitionFit: Enamelled means covered with a coat of enamel.

entries.clue: Neglected, and treated with contempt around university (7)

indicatorNotes.around: around means surrounding, so the contempt word surrounds the university letter

annotation.surface: A student is ignored and scorned on campus.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dissed' is modern slang, short for disrespected.
annotation.definitionFit: Something disused has fallen out of use and been left neglected.

entries.clue: Monk’s function requiring small container (9)

annotation.definitionNote: a Dominican is strictly a friar

blocks.note: a do is a party or function

annotation.surface: A monk's role calls for a little tin.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Function' suggests a purpose; it is the social sort, a do.
annotation.definitionFit: A Dominican is a member of the Order of Preachers founded by St Dominic.

entries.clue: Hotel employee’s dark period overcoming drink? (5,6)

indicatorNotes.overcoming: to overcome is literally to come over, so in a down entry the first piece sits on top

annotation.surface: A hotel worker going through a bad patch beats his drinking habit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dark period' suggests depression, but it is simply night.
annotation.definitionFit: A night porter staffs a hotel's front desk overnight.

entries.clue: Like a mole, for example, eating his grub? (13)

annotation.definition: Like a mole, for example, eating his grub?

blocks.note: the surface pushes a spy; the setter means the burrowing animal
grub reads as food in general, but a mole's grub is literally grubs, insect larvae

annotation.surface: A spy tucks into his lunch.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mole' and 'grub' both suggest a spy eating; the animal's grub is literally grubs, insects and worms.
annotation.definitionFit: Insectivorous means insect-eating, as moles are.

entries.clue: Church musician often representing him as rector (11)

indicatorNotes.representing: read as re-presenting: the letters are presented again in a new order

annotation.surface: The church organist is often cast as the vicar.
annotation.walkthrough: The fodder stays in the church, with a rector, so the scene gives the letters away as little as possible.
annotation.definitionFit: A choirmaster trains and conducts a choir, usually in a church, hence 'often'.

entries.clue: On radio, a youth contributing to panto (7)

indicatorNotes.On radio: radio is heard and never seen, so the words are to be taken by their sound

blocks.note: a lad = a youth, adding = contributing, with the final g dropped

annotation.surface: A radio report of a young person taking part in a Christmas show.
annotation.walkthrough: Panto (pantomime) is a British Christmas stage show for families; this one is a favourite.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Aladdin is one of the best-known pantomimes.

entries.clue: Oaths sure upset a writer! (9)

indicatorNotes.upset: upset literally means knocked over, so the letters are knocked into a new order

annotation.surface: A writer is offended by some swearing.
annotation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark sells 'upset' as the writer's feelings; it is the instruction to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: Authoress is the dated word for a woman author, one kind of writer.

entries.clue: Indian dynasty in the end calling up forgotten reserve troops (5)

indicatorNotes.in the end: in the end means at the last, so take the final letter of 'calling'

blocks.note: the TA, Territorial Army, renamed Army Reserve in 2014

annotation.surface: An Indian royal house eventually calls up reservists nobody remembered.
annotation.walkthrough: The Territorial Army was Britain's volunteer reserve; its old, now-dropped name is what makes it 'forgotten'.
annotation.definitionFit: The Gupta dynasty ruled much of northern India in the 4th to 6th centuries.

entries.clue: Man showing sign of age, perhaps hides key, turning white (9)

indicatorNotes.hides: to hide something is to keep it inside, out of sight

blocks.note: a bent back comes with age
the Esc key on a keyboard

annotation.surface: An elderly man stoops to hide a key as his hair goes white.
annotation.walkthrough: The key is the computer kind, not a door key; 'perhaps' flags that a stoop is only one sign of age.
annotation.definitionFit: Albescent, from Latin albus 'white', means becoming white or whitish.

entries.clue: Unfashionable wear for women in the suburbs (9)

annotation.surface: Frumpy clothing is what suburban women wear.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a dig at suburban dress sense; 'in' is only a link.
annotation.definitionFit: The outskirts are the outer parts of a town, where the suburbs lie.

entries.clue: Eastern lad having administered church without reverberation (9)

indicatorNotes.without: without in its old sense of outside, so these pieces sit outside the lad

annotation.surface: An eastern boy has run a church with no echo.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Without' reads as lacking, but here it means outside, and 'reverberation' then looks like what is missing.
annotation.definitionFit: Resonance is sound prolonged by vibration, near enough a synonym for reverberation.

entries.clue: Start of terrible split about husband’s frugality (6)

indicatorNotes.Start of: the start of a word is its first letter
indicatorNotes.about: about means around, so the split goes around the husband

annotation.surface: A bitter separation starts over a husband's tight-fistedness.
annotation.walkthrough: The first letter and the split together wrap the husband, so 'about' spans both pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: Thrift is careful, frugal use of money.

entries.clue: Aussie native’s note on rook — or cock? (7)

indicatorNotes.on: on means placed on top of, so in a down entry the note sits above the chess piece

blocks.note: te, the seventh note of the scale

annotation.surface: A question of which bird an Australian's note is about.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Aussie native' is a kangaroo. The birds in the surface are misdirection: the rook is a chess piece.
annotation.definitionFit: A rooster is a cock, the male domestic fowl.

entries.clue: Sentence in writing on southern peak’s fulmars, etc (10)

indicatorNotes.in: the sentence is put in the writing, enclosed by it
indicatorNotes.on: on means next to and after, so the writing follows the southern peak

blocks.note: a tor is a rocky peak, as on Dartmoor
bird = prison time, from rhyming slang birdlime = time

annotation.surface: A line written about seabirds on a southern summit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Doing bird' is British slang for serving a prison sentence.
annotation.definitionFit: Storm birds are seabirds such as petrels and fulmars, thought to herald storms.

entries.clue: Heavenly body, not a fat-soluble compound (7)

indicatorNotes.not: 'not a' says the heavenly body is to be taken without its A

annotation.surface: An astronomer insists something is not a star but a chemical.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Not a' reads as a denial; it is an instruction to drop the letter A.
annotation.definitionFit: Steroids are fat-soluble organic compounds such as cholesterol and many hormones.

entries.clue: Moved slowly, finally summoned by hooter (5)

indicatorNotes.finally: finally means at the end, so take the last letter of 'summoned'
indicatorNotes.by: by means beside, so that letter stands next to the hooter

annotation.surface: A car crept forward, called over at last by a horn.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hooter' suggests a car horn, but it is slang for a big nose.
annotation.definitionFit: A car or boat that nosed forward moved slowly and cautiously.

entries.clue: Retired agent is first of heroes to die (6)

indicatorNotes.Retired: to retire is to go back, so REP is reversed

blocks.note: REP, a sales agent, turned back

annotation.surface: A pensioned-off spy is the first of the heroes to be killed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Agent' suggests a spy, but here it is a sales representative.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to perish is to die, usually violently or suddenly.

entries.clue: Having a bouquet prepared for our side only at first (11)

indicatorNotes.prepared: the letters are made ready in a new arrangement

annotation.surface: Flowers are got ready for the home team alone.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bouquet' suggests flowers, but it means a smell, as of wine.
annotation.definitionFit: Odoriferous means giving off a smell, having a bouquet.

entries.clue: Speaker’s perceived environment (5)

indicatorNotes.Speaker’s: the word as a speaker says it

annotation.surface: A speaker describes their surroundings as they see them.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's in 'Speaker's' belongs to the indicator: it is the speaker's version of 'perceived'.
annotation.definitionFit: A scene is a setting or milieu, as in the music scene.

entries.clue: In South Carolina, getting own back for foraging (10)

annotation.surface: A revenge story set in the American South.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In' sounds like a container signal, but nothing goes inside anything: the two pieces simply join.
annotation.definitionFit: Scavenging is searching for food or useful scraps, foraging.

entries.clue: Situated outside entrance to temple, let it remain (4)

indicatorNotes.outside: the situated word is placed outside, wrapping the letter
indicatorNotes.entrance to: the entrance is where you go in first, so take the first letter of 'temple'

annotation.surface: A statue by a temple's door is to be left where it stands.
annotation.walkthrough: Stet is Latin for 'let it stand', the proofreader's mark cancelling a correction.
annotation.definitionFit: Stet, written in a margin, tells the printer to let the original text remain.

entries.clue: Be divided by new term for hardliner (9)

indicatorNotes.divided by: a thing divided by another is split apart by it, so the second piece goes in the middle

annotation.surface: A fresh label is coined for someone uncompromising.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Divided by' sounds like arithmetic; here it means split open to take something in.
annotation.definitionFit: An extremist holds extreme, uncompromising views, which is what a hardliner does.

entries.clue: Choose Italian film about golf: it has drawing power (13)

indicatorNotes.about: about means around, so the Italian goes around the golf letter

blocks.note: G = golf in the phonetic alphabet

annotation.surface: Pick an Italian movie about golf, one with real pulling power.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Italian film' reads as a single thing, a film from Italy, but the two words work separately.
annotation.definitionFit: An electromagnet attracts iron, so it literally has drawing power.

entries.clue: Dress with a certain appeal, primarily round India (4)

indicatorNotes.primarily: primarily means first of all, so take the first letter of 'round'

blocks.note: I = India in the phonetic alphabet

annotation.surface: A garment with allure, mostly worn around India.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A certain appeal' is a coy way of saying sex appeal, a crossword staple.
annotation.definitionFit: A sari is the long draped dress worn by women in South Asia.

entries.clue: Seasonal farm-worker, one hastening to acquire garment (9)

indicatorNotes.to acquire: to acquire a garment is to take it on, so the hastener takes the garment inside

annotation.surface: A farmhand rushes to buy some clothes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'One hastening' is a made-up agent noun from the verb to hare, meaning to run fast.
annotation.definitionFit: A harvester gathers crops at harvest time, work that comes round once a season.

entries.clue: Fool, possibly, principally serving in arid waste (7)

indicatorNotes.principally: principally means chiefly, first, so take the first letter of 'serving'
indicatorNotes.in: the letter is put in the arid waste, surrounded by it

blocks.note: a desert is an arid waste

annotation.surface: A fool, perhaps, stranded and serving in a barren wilderness.
annotation.walkthrough: A fool is a British pudding of fruit folded into cream, so it is an example of the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Fool is a dessert of puréed fruit and cream, so the definition is by example.
